title: A subject discovered late still becomes a column for the students seen earlier
prompt: What does this return? Read it — do not run it.

given.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
var subjects = (payload map $.subject) distinctBy $
---
payload groupBy $.student pluck ((rows, student) -> subjects reduce ((subj, acc = { student: student }) -> acc ++ { (subj): (rows filter ($.subject == subj))[0].score default 0 }))

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
var subjects = (payload map $.subject) distinctBy $
---
payload groupBy $.student pluck ((rows, student) -> subjects reduce ((subj, acc = { student: student }) -> acc ++ { (subj): (rows filter ($.subject == subj))[0].score default 0 }))

explanation.approach: Chem is not discovered until Bo's second record, three rows into the payload, but the discovery pass runs over the whole input before any row is built, so Ada's row — built after discovery — still gets a Chem column, filled with 0.
